audience: United States and global English-speaking NBA and basketball fans
core_topics: draft stories and career turning points
trades and decisions that changed teams
current NBA stories with evergreen narrative value

packaging_strategy.goal: Maximize qualified CTR and retention with strong basketball emotion, recognizable stars and factual curiosity gaps.
title_style: recognizable player or team plus an unresolved contradiction
what happened to a player, team or era
the NBA player who did something extraordinary or unexpected
a strange rule, record, trade or decision explained through a human story
nobody expected this player or team to become what they became
current NBA events reframed as durable stories rather than score recaps
title_avoid: claims about private motives without evidence
titles that depend only on a score and lose relevance within hours

principles: one dominant recognizable player whenever possible
extreme foreground and strong facial expression when relevant
one narrative object such as a ball, jersey, trophy, scoreboard element or arena
clear foreground, midground and background depth
strong visual contrast and mobile readability
use hands, gaze and objects as visual vectors
thumbnail must create curiosity before the title is read

rules: Prioritize NBA subjects with strong recognition in the United States.
Mix evergreen player and team stories with timely NBA opportunities.
Never fabricate trades, injuries, quotes, statistics, scandals, crimes or motives.
Verify statistics, contracts, dates and records with reliable sources before using them.
Clearly separate verified fact from interpretation and fan debate.
Use factual clickbait: aggressive curiosity gaps are encouraged, false promises are not.
Do not rely on unlicensed broadcast footage as the core visual strategy.
The first 20 seconds must establish a contradiction, consequence or unanswered question.
Plant one central reveal loop in the opening and resolve it near the end.
Every 45-90 seconds introduce a new question, reversal, comparison, statistic or consequence.
The ending must resolve the exact promise made by the title and opening hook.
